source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Jun-jun, 15, has had a stepwise-rising fever for a week, headache, and rose spots on his abdomen.
questions.stem: Which disease does the nurse suspect in Jun-jun?
questions.rationale: Typhoid fever begins with headache, nausea and vomiting, a ladder-like (stepwise) fever, and rose spots on the abdomen.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Typhoid Fever (PDF p. 164)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Jun-jun, 15, has had a stepwise-rising fever for a week, headache, and rose spots on his abdomen.
questions.stem: Jun-jun suddenly has right lower abdominal pain and a rigid abdomen. What complication is MOST likely?
questions.rationale: Hemorrhage and perforation are the most dreaded complications. The nurse watches for sudden right lower abdominal pain and abdominal rigidity.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Typhoid Fever (PDF p. 164–165)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which drug should be AVOIDED in a client with bacillary dysentery (shigellosis)?
questions.rationale: Antidiarrheal drugs are contraindicated in shigellosis because they delay fecal excretion of the organism and can prolong fever.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bacillary Dysentery (PDF p. 166)
questions.quote: Contraindicated: Anti-diarrheal drugs (they delay fecal excretion that can lead to prolong fever)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A client from Sorsogon has had blood-streaked sputum for months that does not respond to TB drugs. He often eats raw crabs. What is suspected?
questions.rationale: Paragonimiasis (lung fluke) comes from eating raw or undercooked crabs or crayfish. It causes a long cough and blood-streaked sputum that look like TB but do not respond to TB drugs.
questions.quote: PTB – like signs/symptoms not responding to anti-TB medication

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which lab test is MOST useful for an early presumptive diagnosis of mumps?
questions.rationale: An elevated serum amylase is the most useful test for an early presumptive diagnosis of mumps.
questions.quote: Serum amylase Determination (most useful test in making early presumptive diagnosis of mumps)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.rationale: The 48 hours just before parotid swelling begins is the period of highest communicability. Cases are infectious up to a week before until 9 days after.
questions.quote: 48 – hours period immediately preceding onset of swelling is considered the time of highest communicability.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A child with mumps has painful parotid glands. Which food should the mother AVOID giving?
questions.rationale: Soft, bland, semi-solid food is easier to manage. Acidic foods such as fruit juices increase discomfort.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: After eating home-canned food, a client has double vision, droopy eyelids, and trouble swallowing. Which paralysis pattern is expected?
questions.rationale: Botulism is a neurotoxin illness of descending flaccid paralysis with blurred vision, ptosis, dry mouth, and difficulty swallowing and breathing.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: How should a family make home-canned food safer to eat?
questions.rationale: Clients who eat home-canned food are taught to boil it for 10 minutes before eating to make sure it is safe.
questions.quote: boil the food for 10 minutes before eating to ensure that it is safe to consume.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Before giving botulinum antitoxin, what must the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Before botulinum antitoxin, the nurse checks the client's allergies and does a skin test first.
questions.quote: If giving the botulinus antitoxin, check the patient’s allergies, perform a skin test first.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which stage of Entamoeba histolytica is the infective stage?
questions.rationale: The cyst is the infective stage. It resists environmental conditions and survives a few days outside the body. Trophozoites invade tissue.
questions.quote: Cyst – considered to be the infective stage

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: How should the nurse handle a stool specimen for amoebiasis?
options: Send it to the lab immediately
questions.rationale: No oil preparation for 48 hours before collection; collect a large portion with blood and mucus, label it, and send it to the laboratory immediately.
questions.quote: Send specimen immediately to the laboratory

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which is the intermediate host of Schistosoma japonicum in the Philippines?
questions.rationale: S. japonicum, endemic in the Philippines, uses the snail Oncomelania hupensis quadrasi as its intermediary host. Cercariae penetrate the skin in infested water.
questions.quote: Oncomelania hupensis quadrasi is the intermediary host

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A farmer from Leyte has an itchy rash a day after wading in a rice field. What is this early sign called?
questions.rationale: The first stage of schistosomiasis is a pruritic rash ('swimmer's itch') about 24 hours after cercariae penetrate the skin. Katayama fever comes in the second stage.
questions.quote: Pruritic rash known as “swimmers itch” occurs 24 hours after penetration of cercariae in the skin

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.rationale: The circumoval precipitation test (COPT) is confirmatory for schistosomiasis. Fecalysis, biopsy, and ELISA are also used.
